key_insight: PHO-Agents combines structured EHR prediction with multi-agent LLM reasoning to improve health outcome forecasting and produce clearer explanations.
clinical_relevance: This hybrid approach could support more accurate and interpretable clinical decision support for high-risk patients across multiple real-world settings.
method: Encoded longitudinal EHR sequences into attention-based patient representations and initial logits.
Converted model outputs into patient summaries for an LLM-based data agent.
Used retrieval, research, doctor, and leader agents to review clinical evidence and synthesize a final prediction and explanation, then fused these with the EHR model output.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three real-world cohorts and reported strong gains over single-agent and multi-agent LLM baselines, including PR-AUC 90.20 ± 2.07 for AKI mortality versus 56.46 ± 2.98 for the best single-agent baseline.
watch_item: The approach may be harder to deploy reliably in practice because it depends on high-quality EHR data, guideline retrieval, and coordinated multi-agent LLM behavior.
paper_title: PHO-Agents: A Large Language Model Powered Multi-Agent System for Predicting Health Outcomes
